user.title: Connect EG Austria
user.description:
1. Log in to the member portal {portal_url} in your browser.
2. Open the developer tools (F12) → Application (Firefox: Storage) → Cookies → portal.eg-austria.at.
3. Copy the value of `portal.jwtToken` and paste it here.

Next, Home Assistant offers to create a read-only access token from this cookie, so you don't have to repeat this every month. The cookie itself is not stored. If you already have a personal access token (`ecapi_…`), paste that instead. More: {readme_url}

data_description.token: Value of `portal.jwtToken`. Surrounding quotes and `portal.jwtToken=` are removed automatically.

create_token.title: Create an access token?
create_token.description:
Home Assistant can now create a **read-only** access token named "{token_name}" for your portal account, valid for one year. It can read your energy data but not change anything. EG Austria sends you an email about the new token ("Neuer Access-Token erstellt").

Only the access token is stored, not your session cookie. Without it, Home Assistant keeps the session cookie, which expires in {days} days.

create_failed.title: Access token not created
create_failed.description: Setup continues with the session cookie (valid for about a month). You get a repair warning before it expires; you can try again later with Reconfigure. If EG Austria still sends you an email about a new token, it was created anyway.

token_expiry.title: Personal token expiry
token_expiry.description: The integration can't read the expiry of a pasted personal token. Enter the date you chose when creating it (the portal default is one year). You get a repair warning 30 days before.

data_description.token_expires: Expiry date you chose in the portal when you created the personal token.

expiring_soon.title: Session token expires soon
expiring_soon.description: This session token expires in {days} days. Setup continues, but you will have to paste a new token soon. A personal token avoids this.

reauth_confirm.title: Reconnect EG Austria
reauth_confirm.description:
The stored token was rejected or has expired.

1. Log in to the member portal {portal_url} in your browser.
2. Open the developer tools (F12) → Application (Firefox: Storage) → Cookies → portal.eg-austria.at.
3. Copy the value of `portal.jwtToken` and paste it here.

Next, Home Assistant offers to create a new access token. A personal token (`ecapi_…`) of the same member also works. More: {readme_url}

data_description.token: Value of `portal.jwtToken`, or a personal token (`ecapi_…`) of the same member.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure EG Austria
reconfigure.description: This entry uses an access token that Home Assistant created.

menu_options.reconfigure_token: Change token, metering points or communities

reconfigure_token.title: Reconfigure EG Austria
reconfigure_token.description: Optionally paste a new session cookie (Home Assistant then offers to create a new access token) or a personal token (see {readme_url}). Leave empty to keep the stored token. A token Home Assistant created stays valid until it expires when you replace it; revoke it first if you no longer need it. Next you can change the metering points and add communities.

data_description.token: Value of `portal.jwtToken`, or a personal token (`ecapi_…`). Leave empty to keep the stored token.

revoke_token.title: Revoke the access token
revoke_token.description:
An access token can't revoke itself, so a fresh session cookie is needed.

1. Log in to the member portal {portal_url} in your browser.
2. Open the developer tools (F12) → Application (Firefox: Storage) → Cookies → portal.eg-austria.at.
3. Copy the value of `portal.jwtToken` and paste it here.

Home Assistant then revokes the token it created. Next you can create a new one or keep the session cookie. To stop the integration completely, delete the entry afterwards. More: {readme_url}

data_description.token: Value of `portal.jwtToken` from a fresh portal login. An access token can't be used here.

sources.title: Comparison sources
sources.description: Optional energy statistics from your own meter or inverter, compared with the portal data. Leave a field empty if you don't have that source. The fields are prefilled from the Energy dashboard settings, which this integration never changes.

data_description.source_feed_in: Energy returned to the grid, as measured by your live meter or inverter (kWh total).
data_description.source_grid_consumption: Energy drawn from the grid, as measured by your live meter or inverter (kWh total).
data_description.source_pv: Total energy produced by your PV system (kWh total). Without it, PV cards and values are left out.

error.source_not_statistic: No long-term statistic with a total (sum) found for this. Pick an energy sensor with state class total or total_increasing.
error.source_not_energy: This statistic isn't in an energy unit (Wh, kWh, MWh, …).
error.source_own_statistic: Pick your own meter's statistic here, not one of this integration's.
error.source_duplicate: This statistic is already used in another field.

refetch.name: Re-fetch
refetch.description: Fetches a date range again from the member portal and rewrites its statistics. Runs in the background.

start_date.description: First day to fetch. Default: the daily window (62 days).

end_date.name: End date
end_date.description: Last day to fetch. Default: today. At most 400 days after the start date.

release_held.name: Release held days
release_held.description: Releases days that validation held back, so the next run writes them as the portal sends them.

statistic_key.description: Only this statistic, for example home_generation. Default: all.

date.name: Date
date.description: Only this day. Default: all held days.

token_expiring.title: EG Austria token expires soon
token_expiring.description:
The portal token of {title} expires on {expires} (in {days} days). After that no data is imported until a new token is stored.

Create a new token (a personal access token is recommended) and paste it with **Reconfigure** on the EG Austria integration page. This message disappears once the new token is saved.

api_changed.title: EG Austria portal response changed
api_changed.description:
On {date} a response from the EG Austria portal for {title} did not match the expected format (rules: {rules}). To protect your statistics nothing was written. The integration keeps trying daily and clears this message after a run validates.

Please download the diagnostics of this entry (they are redacted) and attach them to an issue report in the integration's issue tracker.

stale_client.title: EG Austria portal was updated
stale_client.description:
On {date} the EG Austria portal told {title} that the member portal was updated and this client is out of date. To protect your statistics nothing was written. The integration keeps trying daily and clears this message after a run validates.

Check for an update of the integration. If there is none yet, please download the diagnostics of this entry (they are redacted) and attach them to an issue report.

implausible_data.title: EG Austria data held back
implausible_data.description:
Some data for {title} failed a plausibility check and was not written (rules: {rules}; statistics: {statistics}; dates: {dates}). Everything else was imported.

The next run checks these days again and clears this message when they pass. If you have confirmed in the portal that the values are correct, call the action **EG Austria: Release held days** to write them with the next run.

portal_unreachable.title: EG Austria portal unreachable
portal_unreachable.description: The EG Austria portal could not be reached for {title} on {days} consecutive days (last successful import: {last_success}). Imports continue automatically when the portal answers again; no data is lost as long as the portal still offers it.
